events.title: Hiring in the Age of AI
events.description:
What are companies actually looking for when they review your resume? Has the rise of AI coding assistants changed hiring expectations for developers? Are degrees still important? What skills stand out in today's market?

DSM Web Geeks is hosting a panel discussion focused on the current state of hiring in software development and technology roles. Let's share our perspectives on what employers are looking for, how hiring practices are evolving, and how candidates can better position themselves in a rapidly changing industry.

This will be an open conversation with opportunities for audience Q&A, making it a great chance to ask questions about resumes, interviewing, technical skills, career growth, and the impact of AI on hiring.

Whether you're actively job searching, considering your next career move, hiring for your own team, or simply curious about how the technology job market is changing, you'll leave with valuable insights from professionals working in the field every day.

Monday, July 13th
6:30 to 8:00 PM
Hosted at Source Allies and also online.

For those unable to join us physically, worry not! This event, as well as future gatherings, will be expertly streamed on our Twitch channel at [twitch.tv/dsmwebgeeks](https://www.twitch.tv/dsmwebgeeks). Tune in from wherever you are and be a part of the DSM Web Geeks community.

Check out https://www.dsmwebgeeks.com/ for details on this and all future events.

We meet the second Monday of every month. Our topics focus on new trends and techniques in web development.

events.title: Coding Dojo
events.description:
Join the Web Geeks March Meetup on Monday, August 10th, 6:30-8pm at Source Allies for a Coding Dojo!

Are you ready to dive into a collaborative coding challenge and explore new trends and techniques in software development? Web Geeks invites you to our next tech meetup where learning, experimentation, and community are at the forefront.

What’s Happening?
In the spirit of a traditional coding kata done the old-fashioned dojo way, we'll break into groups based on the computers available—so please remember to bring your own laptop. Each group will be given 60 minutes to tackle a fun and challenging coding problem using any means necessary. Whether you're keen to explore a new tech stack, experiment with an unfamiliar framework, or sharpen your TDD skills, this is your opportunity to learn by doing!

The Dojo Experience
Collaborative Challenge: Work with peers in small groups, exchange ideas, and learn from one another as you work through the coding kata.

Safe to Fail, Safe to Learn: At Web Geeks, we value the learning journey over the destination. We're not looking for the perfect solution—just a thoughtful approach and a willingness to experiment.

Community Presentations: At the end of the session, each group will share their results. This isn’t about who got it “right” but about discussing your thought process, the challenges you encountered, and the lessons you learned along the way.

Bring your computer and your curiosity. We will see you in the dojo!

events.title: The Great Migration: An AI-Assisted Journey from TypeScript to Python
events.description:
Migrating an application from one programming language to another has traditionally been a time-consuming and risky process. But what changes when AI becomes part of the development team?
DSM Web Geeks welcomes Daryle Foulke on Monday, September 14th from 6:30-8pm for a look at migrating a TypeScript application to Python with modern AI coding assistants. Through a live demonstration, Daryle will walk through the migration process, showing where AI can accelerate the translation of business logic and application structure and where human expertise remains essential. He’ll also cover some of the challenges developers can encounter along the way, including type-system differences, package ecosystem mismatches, and async programming differences between Node.js and Python.
You’ll learn approaches for prompting AI coding assistants, validating generated code with tests, and breaking a migration into small, verifiable increments.

Speaker Bio: Daryle is a Software Engineer at Source Allies with experience across cloud technologies and full-stack development. His technical background includes AWS, Python, Java, TypeScript, GraphQL, Terraform, and PostgreSQL, along with experience building enterprise software and working directly with clients.

events.title: Hacktoberfest
events.description:
Hacktoberfest 2026: DSM Web Geeks Hack Day

**Let’s get hacking!**
Join DSM Web Geeks on Monday, October 12th at 6:30 PM at Source Allies as we celebrate Hacktoberfest with an evening of open source, collaboration, and coding.

Hacktoberfest is a celebration of open source that brings developers together to contribute, learn, and support the projects and communities that make so much of modern software possible. Whether you’ve contributed to dozens of open source projects or have never opened a pull request before, you’re welcome to join us.

**What’s Happening?**
We’ll kick things off with a quick introduction to contributing to open source, including how to find a project, choose an issue, and work through the contribution and pull request process.

*Then we’ll start hacking!*

Bring your laptop and a project you’d like to contribute to, or join up with other developers at the event. We’ll have time to work individually, pair with others, ask questions, and share what we’re working on.

Have an open source project of your own that could use some help? Bring it! We’d love to give local maintainers a chance to introduce their projects and connect with potential contributors.

You don’t need to be an open source expert to participate. Documentation improvements, bug fixes, tests, accessibility improvements, and small features can all be valuable contributions. This is a chance to learn the contribution process in a friendly environment and meet other developers along the way.

**What to Bring**
Bring a laptop and anything else you need to code comfortably. If you already have a GitHub account, make sure you can log in before the event.

Don’t have a project in mind? That’s okay. We’ll help you find something to work on when you arrive.

*Food and drinks will be provided.*
